newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures scoop late gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures scoop late gains.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures scooped late gains to finish Wednesday broadly higher on good roaster support after earlier trade and light fund selling fizzled out.
Floor traders said soaring New York arabica values on nearby supply worries had little influence in London, the latter being weighed down by good availability of robustas.

"London and New York have different agenda," said one trader. "There may be a bit of tightness of primary robustas like Uganda as the crop is coming to an end but supplies from other robusta areas are still good."
May/May arbitrage against London widened to $1.63 a lb, a new record high, from around the $1.40s in the past few days as the New York contract continued to propel higher.
London's May, which has seen a bout of liquidation ahead of the contract's first tender day on Thursday, managed just $5 up at $1,537 after spending most of the day in the negative territory.
May has been under pressure all week amid concerns over the new grading rules which come into effect with the July.
Traders said players were reluctant to risk taking delivery of May coffee in case they have to re-deliver the material under revised grading terms in July.
July headed much higher towards the close and it finished $22 up at $1,620 after recovering from a low of $1,596.
May/July switch again formed the bulk of the day's volume of 8,806 lots.
The nearby spread was traded at $75 in the afternoon against $70 this morning. Earlier this week, it was traded at around $20-$30.
May's open positions continued to dwindle, dropping by a sizeable 3,157 lots to 4,724 lots by Tuesday's close. But July rose by 2,223 to 20,608.
Activity is expected to slow down on Thursday in view of Labour day holidays in many countries.
New York arabica futures charged higher by midsession, buoyed by speculative buying amid ongoing supply concerns.
U.S. broker Merrill Lynch said in its bi-weekly commodity report that a rally on the New York coffee market could last until September. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
